-3- Service Director Almario M. delos Santos, the Civil Service, in reply to our query on the status of appointments and t rm of office of the Barangay Secretary, Barangay Treasurer and other arang y appointive officials, responded by saying that: "there is no istin Civil Service rule or regulation relative to the appointment of arangay Treasurer, Barangay Secretary and other appointive o/ficials. We believe, however, that by their nature, the same are e •ther coterminus with the appointing authority or co-existent wit the tenure of the appointing authority or at his pleasure' Clearly, therefore, the foregoing app intive barangay officials are considered coterminus with or serving at the ple ure of the appointing authority. Such being the case, these kinds pf offic•als belong to the class of non-career service in government. Thus, eing n n-career, Civil Service eligibility is not a requirement. In the case of Alquizola Sr. vs. Ocol (G.R. o. 132413, 27 August 1999), the Supreme Court ruled that the power of appointment of Barangay Secretary, Barangay Treasurer and other barangay appointive officials is to be exercised conjointly by the Punong Barangay ahd a majority of all the members of the Sangguniang Barangay, the reaSon being that under Section 389 of the Code, the law explic• ly ve ts unto the Punong Barangay, upon approval by a majority f all the members of the Sangguniang Barangay, the power to appoint or replace the Barangay Secretary, Barangay Treasurer and other bara gay a pointive officials. In the same case, the Supreme Court li ewise held that the power of removal is also to be conjointly exercised by thé Punong Barangay and the majority of all the members of the Sangguniang "rangay since the law provides that the removal of these officials inust Iso be subject to the approval of all the members of the Sangguniang Ba angay. The Supreme Court finally declared that: "without such Conjoi action, neither an appointment nor a replacement can be effectua Thus, while technically speaking, these aran ay appointive officials are coterminus with the appointing authority, o a c rtain extent, however, they enjoy security of tenure insofar as the can nly be removed after following the procedures provided for under Yle Lo al Government Code, and that is, to be removed by the Punong Baranga and such removal is approved by the majority of all the members o the S ngguniang Barangay. The e-elec ion of Mayor Tenorio does not revive the lapsed appointment of Mr. Briones. Since the Local Governmen Code did not provide for the minimum, the number of BPSO may be reduc d based on the best judgment of the Punong Barangay. With respect to increasing the numbe of BP O, we believe that your barangay can do so but it should not exceed 2 per Section 393 of the Local Government Code. In fine, replying to your query no. 3 ( ), (b) a d (c), we are of the view that you can increase the number of your BPSO but not to exceed 20 or you can decrease the number of the BPSO and inprease their honoraria but in any event, the 55% personal services limitations under the Local Government Code should always be complied wit . Hence, it can only abolish positions created through a arangay ordinance. The budget, therefore, allocated for offices abolished by the barangay ordinance can be considered as savings of the b rangay.
